name: Gatorback Cycle Park

soil.notes: Old lime-rock quarry site. Riders describe a hard limestone/clay base with sand hauled in over the years, so it rides as a sandy clay rather than a typical deep Florida sand track. Directories variously call it red clay or a hardpack/sand mix; long-time riders consistently say hard limerock-clay base softened by added sand.

layout.notes: Roughly 1.2-mile track with more elevation than most Florida venues, including a drop into the old quarry. Historic big jump known as the Elevator (smaller now than in the 1990s), a triple section, a sandy whoop section in the woods, and a sweeping left near the road that packs hard and slick. Two race tracks can share one start gate.

conditions.dry: Starts tacky and good in the morning when the clay is fresh; as the sun bakes it, it goes hard and slick on the packed sections while the sandy parts break into ruts and bumps.
conditions.wet: Heavy rain has flooded the pits and track during Mini O's week and cancelled racing; after drying, riders reported soft but well-formed ruts. Mud adds deep ruts.
conditions.late_day: Gets very rough in the afternoon; deep ruts and large braking bumps by end of day at big events (photos from 2023 Mini O's showed waist-deep ruts on kids' bikes).
conditions.watering_prep: Prepped and tilled for organized race weekends; sand has been added over time to soften the hard base. No regular open practice, so prep is event-driven.
conditions.seasonal: Main use is winter and Thanksgiving-week events (Florida Winter AM series, Thor Mini O's in late November) plus the Southeast Youth Regional in early June.

rider_reports.says: Several long-time riders agree the base is hard limestone/clay from the old quarry with sand mixed in over the years; one compares the current surface to Budds Creek and says it gets very rough and rutted, another says it is best in the first motos while the clay is fresh and brutal by afternoon.
Riders said Gatorback's dirt was once nearly the same hard clay-limerock mix as Hardrock, but has had a lot of sand mixed in recent years.
Youth regional organizer notes describe the track as softer than it used to be with deep ruts because sand has been worked into the harder dirt.
A racer at Mini O's said that after flooding rain earlier in the week, the track came back better than expected with soft, good ruts and credited the track crew.
Mini O's recap noted mud, very deep ruts and braking bumps bigger than speed bumps, calling the track gnarly late in the week.

gaps: Coordinates come from a directory listing, not the operator
Phone differs between sources ((321) 689-3461 on MX Sports, (407) 473-4373 on MX Parks)
No regular open practice; exact current layout of each track not published
Directory soil labels (red clay) conflict with rider descriptions (limerock/clay with added sand)

name: WW Ranch Motocross Park

soil.notes: Classic Florida sand over a harder base in places, with veins of clay and clay hauled onto many jump faces for consistency. Pros and press consistently call it a sand track; some sections switch abruptly from deep sand to hard base.

layout.notes: DreamTraxx-built national layout on flat ground with some man-made elevation. Wide and fast with big tabletops and doubles, long rhythm and whoop sections and long straights. Corner exits where sand gives way to hard base are the trickiest spots.

conditions.dry: Starts fast, then deep sand ruts and bumps form; front end floats in the deep sand and the rear can hook up suddenly when it hits the hard base underneath.
conditions.wet: Afternoon thunderstorms are common in summer; no detailed rider reports of wet conditions found.
conditions.late_day: Deteriorates through the day into a very rough, rutted sand track; fitness decides late motos.
conditions.watering_prep: Deep-tilled for races (described as shaped like a national). Prepped and watered on its limited riding days.
conditions.seasonal: Summer heat and humidity are severe; hosted the 2017 MXGP of USA and Pro Motocross nationals 2019-2020. Closed to normal open practice; riding by posted days, training groups or races.

rider_reports.says: Race breakdown described a sand-dominant track with clay veins and clay on jump faces, abrupt transitions from deep sand to hard base on corner exits that made the rear tire spin up, and a track that got very rough and wore riders down by the second moto.
A former Florida pro previewing the national called it typical Florida: flat, sandy and rough, with limited man-made elevation and heat as the main challenge.
Amateur race report said the crew tilled the pro track for amateurs and it got as rough as a national; younger riders found it rougher than their usual tracks.
A pro quoted in the MXGP announcement called it a classic Florida sand track with clay jumps and dark sand straights that starts fast and gets rough.
Local riders note it is the biggest track near Jacksonville but closed to open practice; check the website for riding days.

name: Bostwick Creek MX Park
address: 1350 Sungarden Rd, Green Cove Springs, FL 32043

soil.notes: Dark black loam on the motocross tracks with clay in the jump faces, unusual for Florida where deep sand is the norm; a separate GP-style sand track. Several independent listings agree on black loam.

layout.notes: About 60 acres. Main track has a permanent rhythm section, tabletops, bowl turns and singles; roughly a two-minute lap for A riders. Mostly small jumps with some large ones; trees and shade around the property.

conditions.dry: Loam rides soft and grippy when watered; how it holds up depends on watering and traffic.
conditions.watering_prep: Tracks listed as watered and groomed.
conditions.seasonal: Practice typically Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday; hours vary with season, track work and weather.

rider_reports.says: Riders recommended Bostwick as a must-ride and called it fun; one 2019 poster said it had not been open for a while at that time.
Recommended as fun for a holiday ride, though its holiday opening was uncertain.

name: North Florida Motocross Park

soil.notes: Red clay with loam and a little sand. Two directories agree on red clay/loam and a rider calls the dirt good.

layout.notes: Around 35 acres. Main track is about a mile with wide turns and jump sections sized for novices and vets; the Outback track is a rhythm-focused loop of rollers and technical corner combinations. Riders call the jumps very small and the lap short.

conditions.wet: Listing notes some mud after rain.
conditions.watering_prep: Closed midweek days for rebuilding, grooming and watering; prep varies by practice/event date.
conditions.seasonal: Weekend practice plus a midweek day; hours have changed over time, confirm before going.

rider_reports.says: Jacksonville riders said NFMX is the closest track, fun, with good dirt, but has very small jumps and a short lap that can get boring.

name: Decker Training Facility at County Line MX

soil.notes: Sand and clay mix on rolling ground; one listing says mostly sand, another a clay/sand mix, plus a dedicated sand training track. Riders call the dirt good.

layout.notes: About 1.25-mile pro track with notable elevation change for Florida; riders call it a big layout. Hosted AMA Pro ATVMX in March 2026, described as fast and technical.

conditions.wet: Weather dependent; riders report rain-outs closing it.
conditions.watering_prep: Riders describe it as fully prepped; listed as watered and groomed.
conditions.seasonal: Training compound built for camps and multi-day stays; historically reduced riding in July-September heat. Access may be limited to on-site riders, camp attendees or scheduled public practice.

rider_reports.says: Panhandle riders called County Line a top local track with a big layout and good dirt, fully prepped, improving each year, but weather dependent and sometimes closed in late summer.
ATVMX national report called the layout fast and technical and hard on machine setup and fitness.

name: MX 191

soil.notes: Clay and sand mix; a rider review calls it a near-perfect blend where sand keeps corners rough and clay keeps jump faces from rutting. One directory also mentions heavy loam.

layout.notes: Flowing layout with forgiving jumps (30 to 90 ft per early description) that can be cased safely; little elevation. Lap of roughly 1 to 1.5 minutes. Kept rough on purpose, with a Midwest feel.

conditions.dry: Stays moist thanks to irrigation; sandy corners get rough.
conditions.late_day: Rough, deep rolling bumps develop; treated as an endurance-training track.
conditions.watering_prep: Electronic irrigation across the layout that can wet sections while riders are on track; split big-bike and mini sessions.
conditions.seasonal: Wednesday afternoons and weekends, weather permitting; check social media before going.

rider_reports.says: Rider review scored dirt and prep 10/10: ideal clay-sand blend, in-ride irrigation keeps moisture, kept rough like a Midwest track; layout flows, jumps are safe to case, little elevation, shaded pits.
Recommended by a forum poster for Pensacola-area riding.
